# Migration - Bottom Up, With Dependencies

This simple examples uses two JAR files and a 3rd-party dependency as shown in
the following table.

| Jar File                    | JAR Type | Loaded As | Dependencies                      | Main Method |
| --------------------------- | -------- | --------- | --------------------------------- | :---------: |
| `app.jar`                   | Regular  | Unnamed   | `domain.jar` and `h2-2.5.250.jar` |   **YES**   |
| `domain.jar`                | Regular  | Named     | None                              |     No      |
| `h2-2.5.250.jar`            | unknown  | Unnamed   | None                              |     No      |

In the bottom-up migration, we start from the dependencies. We will start from
the H2.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

## Run the example

1. Build the application

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JAR files were created and copied to the
   `./target/libs` and `./target/mods` directories.

   ```shell
   tree --dirsfirst --sort=name --prune -P '*.jar' './target'
   ```

   The application JAR files

   ```
   ./target
   ├── libs
   │   ├── app.jar
   │   └── h2-2.5.250.jar
   └── mods
       └── domain.jar

   3 directories, 3 files
   ```

2. List all modules

   ```shell
   java --module-path './target/mods' --list-modules
   ```

   The H2 database JAR file is an example of an *automatic* module. Although it
   lacks a `module-info.java`, it can be placed on the module path, where it
   will be assigned an automatic module name based on the `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF`
   file.

   ```shell
   unzip -p './target/libs/h2-2.5.250.jar' 'META-INF/MANIFEST.MF'
   ```

   Although there is no `module-info.class` file, Java recognises that the H2
   JAR contains several packages. The module name is not `h2`—as might be
   expected if it were derived from the JAR filename—ass this JAR include the
   `Automatic-Module-Name` in the `MANIFEST.MF` file.

   The H2 JAR file includes an implementation of `java.sql.Driver`, specified in
   the `META-INF/services/java.sql.Driver` file. This was the standard method
   for Java to discover implementations via the
   [Java Service Provider](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/sound/SPI-intro.html)
   before the introduction of the module system.

   ```shell
   unzip -p './target/libs/h2-2.5.250.jar' 'META-INF/services/java.sql.Driver'
   ```

   The class that provides an implementation for the `java.sql.Driver`

   ```
   org.h2.Driver
   ```

   Describe the `domain.jar` file

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/mods/domain.jar'
   ```

   The domain module description

   ```
   demo.domain@1.0.0 jar:file:///./target/mods/domain.jar!/module-info.class
   exports demo.domain
   requires java.base mandated
   contains demo.domain.formatter
   ```

   Describe the `app.jar` file

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/app.jar'
   ```

   The application module description

   ```
   No module descriptor found. Derived automatic module.

   app automatic
   requires java.base mandated
   contains demo.app
   main-class demo.app.Main
   ```

4. Run the application

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/*' \
     --module-path './target/mods' \
     demo.app.Main
   ```

   Our application starts from the *unnamed* module. The Java Module System has
   no means to build a module dependency tree, and thus only the `java.base` is
   loaded.

   ```
   Connecting to database
   Listing quotes
   Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: demo/domain/Quote
       at demo.app.Main.listQuotes(Main.java:33)
       at demo.app.Main.lambda$main$0(Main.java:15)
       at demo.app.Main.acceptConnection(Main.java:54)
       at demo.app.Main.main(Main.java:12)
   Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: demo.domain.Quote
       at java.base/jdk.internal.loader.BuiltinClassLoader.loadClass(BuiltinClassLoader.java:580)
       at java.base/java.lang.ClassLoader.loadClass(ClassLoader.java:490)
       ... 4 more
   ```

   Add the `demo.domain` module using the `--add-modules` command line option.

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/*' \
     --module-path './target/mods' \
     --add-modules demo.domain \
     demo.app.Main
   ```

   This time the application works and prints the following.

   ```
   Connecting to database
   Listing quotes
   Printing the contents of the quotes table
    - “Learn from yesterday, live for today, hope for tomorrow. The important thing is not to stop questioning.” by Albert Einstein
   ```

5. (*Optional*) Load the `h2-2.5.250.jar` from the module path as an *automatic*
   module.

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/app.jar' \
     --module-path './target/mods/domain.jar:./target/libs/h2-2.5.250.jar' \
     --add-modules demo.domain \
     demo.app.Main
   ```

   The H2 automatic module does not need to be explicitly included. As it
   provides a service (an implementation of `java.sql.Driver`), the module is
   automatically loaded and the implementation made available.

   ```
   Connecting to database
   Listing quotes
   Printing the contents of the quotes table
    - “Learn from yesterday, live for today, hope for tomorrow. The important thing is not to stop questioning.” by Albert Einstein
   ```
